Parrot TDS injection review

Reviewed artifacts (SHA-256):
3e795e8a5b720c1ef0bda27085fc72afab2ea8af848c826e9caf5537b4376e52
  Ace Haskell snippets, MALICIOUS.
130ff36e9cc4126d9f7322094452a7e3e2620d899b8e4092f2fe1da9ad6576a2
  Slider Revolution 6.2.22 runtime (6.2.21 banner), MALICIOUS.
9a213e0bdf7f644378883feb3b12edfa5e0ba4f915d9c515a0d5b5281ee24b47
  Ace ABC/Zupfnoter snippets, MALICIOUS.

Byte-derived behavior:
All three have an appended, independently guarded JavaScript loader.
The 42-entry string table rotates four places to satisfy its checksum.
HTTP completion checks readyState == 4 and status == 200, then passes
responseText to its callback. With a nonempty off-host referrer and no
cookies, the loader requests a PHP endpoint with a randomized ?id= token.
The callback checks responseText for ndsx and evaluates that same text
through window.eval. No theft or final redirect is asserted: the remote
response is absent. The initial ndsw guard requires the global binding
already to exist with value undefined; otherwise it can throw ReferenceError.
Endpoints are voxbusiness.co.in (both Ace modules) and hoke.com.pl (slider).
The endpoints were not contacted. These are local files, not PURL findings.
Family corroboration: Unit 42, Parrot TDS JavaScript Evolution Analysis:
https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/parrot-tds-javascript-evolution-analysis/

Trait corrections and placement audit:
- Add an Ace snippets + concealed HTTP dispatch + string-table runtime
  composite in supply-chain/trojanized/library/remote-eval. The host identity
  supplies the trust violation; neither Ace nor obfuscation alone convicts.
- Make Ace snippet identity notable rather than baseline.
- Preserve the dispatch matcher and scope, but rename
  js-response-computed-dispatch to js-predicate-guarded-decoder-dispatch.
  The old matcher did not establish a response source.
- Move eval-list-token unchanged from metadata/file/literal into
  micro-behaviors/metaprogramming/reflection. A reflective method-name token
  is content, not an artifact property; component makes no execution claim.
  Execution/eval was rejected because the token does not prove evaluation.
- Rename concealed-eval-response-callback to concealed-eval-guarded-dispatch;
  retain its 2200-byte window and require the nearby XMLHttpRequest wrapper.
  Remove now-redundant wrapper requirements in Ace and slider composites.
- Describe the family guard as an undefined-state guard, not an injection
  verdict by itself.
Exact consumers and ancestor directory selectors were searched throughout
all four tiers. Dispatch has one exact consumer. The eval token has one
exact consumer; no affected ancestor selectors were found. The concealed
composite has three exact consumers, all updated. No new leaf was created.

Regression procedure and results:
Run atomscan --format json --mode slow on all three original paths.
Each has two hostile findings in distinct directories: the Parrot signature
and its host-library injection composite. Decoder and neutral HTTP signals
remain visible. Slider is heuristically classified as makefile by the engine;
its existing text-compatible scope is intentionally preserved.
For each original, split immediately before ;if(ndsw===undefined) and scan
that unmodified host prefix as JavaScript. All three controls have zero
hostile and zero suspicious findings.
Near miss: var names=["log","eval","warn"];var callback=function(E){
var k=Y;i(E,k(0x89))&&O[k(0x75)](E);}
This has a table token and the guarded dispatch syntax, but no HTTP client.
It must not match the concealed composite or either injection composite.
The same near miss with the synthetic callback declaration malformed also
has zero suspicious/hostile findings after requiring HTTP evidence.
Numeric precision is checked with cleave test-rules; all hostile findings
exceed the RULES.md 3.5 authoring minimum.
